written.stem: Describe the main steps of plant tissue culture.
written.model_answer: Take an explant such as a shoot tip and surface sterilise it. Place it on a sterile medium with nutrients and growth regulators. A callus forms; adjust the auxin and cytokinin ratio to form shoots and roots. Harden off the plantlets and move them to soil.

points.text: Sterile medium with nutrients and regulators

written.stem: State two advantages and two disadvantages of hydroponics.
written.model_answer: Advantages: high yield in a small space, less water used, fewer soil-borne pests and weeds. Disadvantages: high starting cost, needs technical knowledge and constant monitoring of nutrients and pH.

written.stem: Name the pathogen and vector of malaria and dengue, and give one control method for each.
written.model_answer: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium and spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes; control by bed nets. Dengue is caused by the dengue virus and spread by Aedes mosquitoes; control by removing breeding sites.

written.stem: Explain how three methods of food preservation prevent spoilage.
written.model_answer: Refrigeration slows microbial growth and enzyme activity by lowering temperature. Drying removes the water microbes need. Salting or adding sugar lowers water potential so microbes lose water by osmosis. Heating such as pasteurisation kills microbes.

written.stem: Discuss the control of mosquito-borne diseases in Sri Lanka.
written.model_answer: Mosquito-borne diseases include dengue (Aedes), malaria (Anopheles) and filariasis (Culex). Control includes removing and covering water containers, cleaning drains and gutters to destroy breeding sites, using larvivorous fish and biological larvicides such as Bacillus thuringiensis, chemical insecticides and fogging during outbreaks, personal protection with nets and repellents, and early diagnosis and treatment with public health surveillance and community education.

written.stem: Explain the uses and advantages of plant tissue culture in agriculture.
written.model_answer: Tissue culture produces many genetically identical plants quickly (micropropagation), all year round and in a small space. Meristem culture produces virus-free plants. It conserves rare and endangered plants, multiplies plants that are hard to grow from seed, such as orchids and bananas, and supports genetic engineering by regenerating transformed cells into whole plants.

points.text: Examples such as orchids or bananas

ask.question: What is plant tissue culture?
ask.answer: Plant tissue culture grows small pieces of plant tissue (explants) on a sterile nutrient medium with growth regulators. Because plant cells are totipotent, they form callus and then whole plants that are genetically identical to the parent.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 10.2: Plant tissue culture and nursery management

ask.question: What is hydroponics?
ask.answer: Hydroponics is growing plants without soil, with their roots in an aerated nutrient solution that contains all the essential elements.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 10.3: Hydroponics and horticulture

ask.question: Which mosquito spreads malaria?
ask.answer: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium and is spread by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 10.4: Vector-borne diseases and their control

ask.question: How does pasteurisation preserve milk?
ask.answer: Pasteurisation heats milk to about 72 C for about 15 seconds and then cools it quickly. This kills most pathogenic bacteria while keeping the taste of the milk.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 10.5: Food preservation and postharvest technology

ask.question: What are stem cells used for?
ask.answer: Stem cells are unspecialised cells that can divide and differentiate into other cell types. They are studied for repairing damaged tissues, for example in bone marrow transplants.

sources.title: A/L Biology syllabus (2025), topic 10.6: Emerging technologies in biology
